entry.title: When parents live apart
entry.summary: Both books recognize families whose parents live in different homes. Their preference for contact with both parents is explicitly qualified by the child’s safety.
entry.cue: For understanding the books’ perspective on separated family life.
detail: The Baby authors acknowledge that separation may not have been chosen and that staying together can be unhappy or dangerous. Davies describes the possibility of a workable arrangement, while making the child’s safety the first priority and excluding contact where there is a psychological or physical reason against it.
Both books ask adults to keep their conflict off the child and find adult support for their own difficulties. The child is not asked to carry the disagreement between parents.
In The Montessori Toddler, Davies also emphasizes predictability and factual, age-appropriate updates about changes, without giving the child all the adult details.

principle.text: Family circumstances differ; the child’s safety qualifies continued contact.
